newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: IAMA positive on Australian grain crop.
newsitem.headline: IAMA positive on Australian grain crop.

text.p: Rural merchandiser IAMA Ltd said it remained positive about Australia's grain crop, despite weather forecasters' predictions of a downturn due to the El Nino weather phenomenon.
IAMA was also confident that an excellent start to the current season in three Australian states would see the group's June quarter sales likely to exceed budget.
"The excellent start to the season in three states has already pushed our sales figures above budget," managing director Danny Bourke said in a statement.

Bourke said major cropping areas between Queensland and the northern Victorian border, as well as parts of Western Australia, showed no significant chance of drier weather, based on Bureau of Meteorology reports.
This was despite Bureau forecasts earlier of drier weather for parts of eastern Australia, due to the effects of El Nino.
Large areas in western Queensland and stretching down into New South Wales contained stored moisture through fallowing, which would be beneficial, Bourke said.
"Much of this cropping area which accounts for more than one third of our sales of crop inputs nationally is largely immune from the threat of moisture shortage," he said.
Western Australia, Queensland and much of New South Wales had received excellent rainfall to date, Bourke said.
Also significant was the widespread movement among farmers towards moisture conservation techniques such as chemical fallow and minimal tillage crop establishment, he said.
Iama reported a net profit of A$6.81 million for the six months to March 31 on sales of A$419.28 million.

Australia's key commodities forecaster, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) earlier this month downgraded its forecast for Asutralia's 1997/98 wheat crop to 16.25 million tonnes from its previous forecast of 19.2 million tonnes due to El Nino.
